children: Shares of Newsmax jumped after the company swung to a profit and reported revenue ahead of analyst expectations in the third quarter.
The stock jumped 13% to $8.25 in after-hours trading on Thursday. Shares closed down 5.8% at $7.29, down 5.7% year-to-date.
The media company on Thursday reported a profit of $15.2 million, or 12 cents a share, compared with a loss of $4.1 million, or 3 cents a share, a year earlier.

Revenue rose to $69 million from $45.3 million a year prior. The figure includes $14 million of recognized revenue connected to a one-time service revenue termination payment of an advertising purchase agreement with a customer, Newsmax said. Excluding that, revenue would have risen 22% to $55 million.
Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting the company to post a loss of 1 cent a share on $49.8 million in revenue.

"Setting aside the one-time revenue item, we delivered our fastest revenue growth since our listing and a second consecutive profitable quarter," Chief Executive Christopher Ruddy said. "Engagement rose through the midterm campaign and that is an early indicator of what is ahead."
The company updated its full-year revenue guidance to a range of $226 million to $230 million to account for the one-time revenue item, while keeping its underlying growth guidance unchanged.
